description: This case study is the final report of the joint US-Canada Power System Outage Task Force on the blackout of 14 August 2003, the cascading failure that cut power to about 50 million people in the Midwest and Northeast United States and Ontario, according to the report listings. The report, whose contents run from the electric system and sequence of events to causes, the nuclear and security analyses and recommendations, was published in April 2004 with a cover letter from the US Secretary of Energy and Canada's Minister of Natural Resources. It concludes that the blackout could have been prevented and calls for mandatory reliability rules with substantial penalties; listing summaries name four cause groups, system understanding, situational awareness, tree trimming and reliability coordinator diagnostics. Access: free PDF via the Department of Energy page and copies in the Internet Archive and the OSTI ETDE collection; no licence is stated. Coverage is the northeastern North American interconnection. Caveats: only the cover letter and contents were read here, and the cause statements come from listing summaries. It suits cascading failure and resilience studies of transmission systems, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: The Task Force found that the blackout could have been prevented and states that compliance with reliability rules must be made mandatory with substantial penalties. Its listing summaries name four groups of causes: inadequate system understanding, inadequate situational awareness, inadequate tree trimming and inadequate reliability coordinator diagnostic support, and it recommends mandatory reliability standards and stronger physical and cyber security.
